note: Table of contents (Saheth-Maheth, Sarnath, Bodh-Gaya); no argument.

author: Taw Sein Ko (quoted by Marshall)
asr_identification: Srikshetra = Yathemyo ('City of the Hermit'), ruins 5 miles E of Prome, Hmawza railway station (Prome district, Burma)
evidence: trial excavations at Hmawza 1907-08: ramparts, walled enclosures, Bawbawgyi and other pagodas; votive tablet with Nagari legend of Aniruddha (Anawrata); gold scrolls with the Buddhist creed in 7th-10th c. script from Lehawp; Gupta-style sculpture (Zegu pagoda)
quote: Prome or Si ikshetra was founded by King Duttahaung loi vears after the Nirvana of the Buddha … as it was knowm to the celebrated Chinese pilgrims Hiuen Thsang and 1-tsmp … The site of Srikshetra is noAV called Yathemyo, the ‘ City of the Hermit,' and is five miles to the east of Prome
note: Xuanzang's hearsay country 室利差呾羅 (juan 10) placed at the Hmawza ruins near Prome — same as Mizutani's identification; first excavation report on the site. Marshall (ed.) dates the sculpture to the 7th c. or earlier, i.e. Xuanzang's time.
Sarnath 1908: monastery I-IV architecture and minor finds; Kasia only as architectural comparison; no location argument.

author: Marshall
asr_identification: Jagat Singh Stupa (= Dharmarajika), Sarnath (Benares district)
evidence: trench on N side: walled pradakshina 60 ft from centre with four openings; section of eight building phases, the original stupa of wedge-shaped bricks (c. 19x14x2.5 in.) dated to Asoka, enlarged in Kushana/early Gupta, 5th-6th c., 9th-10th c., 12th c.
quote: In spite of all the attention given to the Jagat Singh Stupa by previous e^iplorers, ever since it was first opened up in 1794 … The original sffijxi (1, yellow) dites back, we believe, to the time of A^oka
note: Does not name the pilgrim, but the Asokan date of the core supports Mizutani's identification of the Asoka stupa W/NW of the vihara (07.01.03) with the Dharmarajika (Jagat Singh) stupa; the survey's ASR coding has no entry for this id.

author: Marshall; Konow (inscriptions)
evidence: inscriptions from the 1908 season: Sarvastivadin inscription (2nd-3rd c.) on the stairs of the Jagat Singh stupa and on the rail in the S chapel of the Main Shrine; Sammitiya inscription on the Asoka pillar; 10th-c. inscription naming the 'Dharmachakra' as the Sarnath monastery; nine new stupas N of the Main Shrine
quote: The Saivastivadins are an offshoot of the orthodox Sthaviravada, just as the Sammitiyasj who have left an inscription on the A§oka pillard … Dharmachakra is known as rhe name of the Sarnath monastery or a shrine within it
note: Epigraphic name of the establishment (Dharmachakra) confirms Sarnath = 鹿野伽藍 (Mizutani agrees; survey agrees). The Sammitiya inscription on the pillar matches Xuanzang's 1,500 monks of the Sammatiya school at the Deer Park.

author: Konow; Vogel
asr_identification: Sarnath = Dharmachakra; Maheth = Sravasti and Saheth = Jetavana (Gonda/Bahraich districts)
evidence: Kumaradevi inscription (12th c.) from Sarnath naming the Dharmachakrajina image and Dharmachakra-jina-vihara; review of earlier work at Saheth-Maheth: Kushana inscription of Friar Bala on the colossal Bodhisattva found by Cunningham, naming Sravasti and the Kosamba-kuti; Hoey's finds (Vidyadhara inscription of 1119, seals); V. A. Smith's counter-identification of Sravasti in Nepal
quote: there was an old image of the Buddha in Sarnath, known as the Dharmachakrajma … Sir A. Cunningham first excavated the mounds of Maheth and Saheth which he identified as the site of the ancient city of SravastI (Pali Savatthi) and that of the Jetavanaj … to have discovered the true site of Sravasti between the villages of Balapur, Karhdi and Intava in Nepal territory
note: Vogel's introduction states the dispute (Cunningham vs. V. A. Smith's Balapur site in Nepal) that the 1907-08 dig was to settle; result in passage 114. Mizutani: Sravasti = Sahet-Mahet (agreed); Jetavana has no identification in Mizutani's table.

author: Vogel
name_in_asr: royal precincts of Sravasti; stupa of Sudatta; place where Devadatta was engulfed
asr_identification: Maheth = the 'royal precincts' (walled inner city, circuit 17,250 ft); Kachchi Kuti not Sudatta's stupa (Brahmanical temple); Baitara Gate not Devadatta's pit
evidence: new survey of Maheth: circuit 17,250 ft (Cunningham 17,300), ramparts 25-40 ft, gates tested by cuttings (Baitara, Pipara, Galhi, Imli gates), Galhi gate 1,386 ft from Saheth; Kachchi Kuti excavated: terracotta panels with Ramayana scenes (Hanuman) show it was a Brahmanical (Vishnu?) temple
quote: Cunningham is, therefore, quite right in asserting that the circuit of 20 It of ‘‘ these royal precincts ” closely agrees with that of the ancient site of Maheth … the conclusion arrived at disposes of Cunningham’s and Dr. Hoey’s attempts to identifv the Kachcln Kuti with one of the Buddhist monuments described by Hiuen Tsian^^ in the city of Sravasti
note: new = Sudatta's house stupa and Devadatta's pit in Sravasti (not in the table). Confirms Maheth = city (Mizutani agrees) on the circuit; rejects Cunningham's Kachchi Kuti = Sudatta stupa (ASR 01) and Hoey's identifications; Vogel holds that individual monuments cannot yet be identified since the ruins reflect the 12th-c. city.

author: Vogel
asr_identification: Pakki Kuti (Cunningham) or Stupa A on the N rampart of Maheth (Hoey); Vogel: no identification possible
evidence: Pakki Kuti excavated: quadrangular brick stupa base, 120 x 77 ft, earthenware ring-drains; Stupa A: solid brick stupa forming one mass with the rampart, top cleared
quote: General Cunninsfham proposed to identify 1 Ids mound with the Ai'igulimala Stupa of the Chinese pilgrims … General Cunningham, as Mr, Vincent Smith remarks, was in any case right in calling the building a stupa; no further identification is at present possible … This monument Dr. Hoey^ proposes to identify with the Angulimdla Stufa mentioned bv Hiuen Tsiang
note: new = Angulimala stupa in Sravasti (not in the table). Withholds Cunningham's Pakki Kuti = Angulimala (ASR 01) and Hoey's Stupa A; Jain temple Sobhnath (Sambhavanatha's birthplace) also described.

author: Vogel; Spooner (Takht-i-Bahi)
asr_identification: Saheth = Jetavana, Maheth = Sravasti (Gonda/Bahraich); Takht-i-Bahi (Mardan, Peshawar district) not mentioned by the pilgrims
evidence: copper plate of Govindachandra of Kanauj, Samvat 1186 (A.D. 1130), found packed in a brick case under the floor of cell 23 of Convent No. 19 at Saheth, granting six villages to the friars 'residing in the great convent of the holy Jetavana'; some granted villages still bear their names; temples 1-3 and the cankrama/Kosamba-kuti; inscribed parasol post of Friar Bala in Lucknow Museum
quote: it conclusively settles the identification of Saheth with the Jetavana-mahavihara and consequently that of Maheth with the city of Sravasti … there can be no reasonable doubt that the site of Saheth represents the Jetavana and consequently that of Maheth the city of Sravasti … the fact remains that the Chinese pilgrims do not mention it
note: Decisive epigraphic confirmation of Cunningham (ASR 01) against V. A. Smith's Nepal site: Jetavana (06.01.04, no identification in Mizutani's table) = Saheth. Vogel also judges the pilgrims' route data from Kausambi (Kia-shi-po-lo, Pi-so-kia unidentified) and Kanauj too uncertain to overturn epigraphy. Spooner (Takht-i-Bahi section) follows Foucher: no pilgrim mentions Takht-i-Bahi — against the survey's reading of it as the mountain near 02.04.16.
Gandhara iconography (Bodhi tree scenes); no location.
Gandhara iconography; Mathura/Sravasti only as art-historical references.

author: Venkayya (Epigraphy section, unsigned)
evidence: summary of the Govindachandra copper plate (Samvat 1186) found in a cell of the SW monastery at Saheth
quote: One of the finds during the excavations at Sahelh-Maheth is a copper-plate of Govindachandra … this copperplate inscription establishes the identity of Saheth- Mahgth with Sravasti
note: Repeats Vogel's result (passage 114) in the epigraphy review. Bears on Mizutani as in 114.

author: Vogel (general review); Spooner
name_in_asr: Kanishka's stupa, Kanishka-chaitya, Shah-ji-ki-Dheri; Purushapura; Sravasti; Jetavana
asr_identification: Kanishka's stupa = E mound of Shah-ji-ki-Dheri outside the Ganj Gate of Peshawar; his monastery = the great W mound; Maheth/Saheth = Sravasti/Jetavana
evidence: Foucher's identification tested by Spooner's excavation 1908-09 (relic casket found, see 146); the two mounds' relative position (stupa E, monastery W) as in the pilgrims; Sappers and Miners' dig 1875 found Buddhist remains burnt by fire; octagonal Hindu temple N of the site where the pipal tree is to be sought; at Saheth a fourth inscription (Mathura sculptor's Bodhisattva) names Sravasti and the Jetavana
quote: conflrins moreover the identity of the ancient sites of MaJieth and Saheth with the famous city of SravastI and the adjoining Buddhist establishment … In this he drew attention to two large mounds outside the Ganj Gate of Posban ar City Avhich seemed to him to answer veiy closely to the accounts … Cunningham had pievioutily iilcntilicd Kanishka s monument with tho Oor Katri in Peshawar City
note: Agrees with Mizutani on 02.04.03. Differs on 02.04.06: Mizutani 'possibly Gor Khattri' (Cunningham's published view, survey asr column) vs. the W mound at Shah-ji-ki-Dheri; Vogel's footnote [E.] records that Cunningham himself later (unpublished, 1875) moved Kanishka's monument to Shah-ji-ki-Dheri — a revision of Cunningham. Distance discrepancy noted: Song Yun 7 li E vs. Xuanzang 8-9 li SE.

author: Spooner
name_in_asr: Kanishka's stupa (pagoda); Kanishka's vihara in the sangharama of Mahasena
asr_identification: Shah-ji-ki-Dheri, outside the Ganj Gate, Peshawar: stupa = E mound, monastery = W mound
evidence: diagonally opposite corners of the stupa found (largest stupa in India); relic chamber at the centre: bronze casket with Kharoshthi inscription 'Agisala, overseer of works at Kanishka's vihara in the sangharama of Mahasena', six-sided crystal reliquary with three bone fragments, sealing with elephant, coin of Kanishka; crowded small stupas SE and E of the main stupa
quote: thercliy confirmed the theory as to its identity … arc undoubtedly the original relics deposited in the stffjm ])y Kanislika Avhich Hiuen-Thsang tells us Avcrc i*elics of Gautama Buddha … The gigantic monastery of which Hinen-Thsang sj)eaks, and of which we seem to have definite traces on the west of the pagoda … This all agrees, therefore, very well indeed Avitli Avhat Hiuen-Tlisang tells us
note: Inscription names Kanishka: confirms Mizutani's 02.04.03 (who cites this dig). For 02.04.06 Spooner puts Kanishka's monastery W of the stupa at Shah-ji-ki-Dheri, not Gor Khattri (Mizutani, uncertain; survey asr = Gor-Katri). Small stupas lack the rich decoration Xuanzang describes.

author: Daya Ram Sahni
evidence: new inscribed Bodhisattva from Marshall's 1908-09 excavations at Saheth; palaeography dated before Kanishka by comparison with Friar Bala's Sravasti and Sarnath Bodhisattvas
quote: They exhibit a certain degree of similarity to the alphabet used in the inscriptions on the Sravasti Bodhisattva referred to above and the similar statue at Sarnath
note: Beginning of Sahni's edition of the Jetavana inscription; the text naming Sravasti and the Jetavana and his conclusion are in passage 160.

author: Daya Ram Sahni; Bloch (Bodh Gaya)
evidence: pre-Kushana Brahmi inscription on a Bodhisattva from Saheth: gift of Kshatriya brothers (Sivadhara...) of Mathura 'in the Jetavana of Sravasti', made by Sivamitra, sculptor of Mathura
quote: “A Bodhisattva [has been set uii] iii tlie Jetavana of Sravasti [as a] gift of … it supplies further authentic evidence in support of the identification of Sahefh-Mahctli with Sravasti … This iclentificatioii is now a settled fact
note: Fourth epigraph confirming Cunningham's Saheth-Maheth = Sravasti/Jetavana (ASR 01); fills the gap in Mizutani's table for 06.01.04. The rest of the passage is Bloch on the history of the Bodhi tree (Sasanka), no location.

author: Bloch
name_in_asr: enclosing walls of the Bodhi Tree; stone railing
asr_identification: Bodh Gaya: the old stone railing (2nd c. B.C.) originally stood round the Bodhi Tree; Xuanzang's enclosure was a brick wall
evidence: railing inscriptions (Indragnimitra, Brahmamitra; Sunga period) date the older railing to the mid-2nd c. B.C.; Bharhut relief shows a wall round the tree
quote: as Hiuen Tsiang ' tells us, Avere “ built of bricks, high and strong ; the enclosure Avas long from east to aa est … It seems most likely that this railing originally stood around the Bodhi Tree
note: Bears on Mizutani's gloss 'enclosure = railing round the temple': Bloch separates the stone railing (round the tree) from the brick enclosure Xuanzang describes. No change of site.

author: Bloch
asr_identification: temple = the present Bodh Gaya temple; Mahabodhi sangharama = the high plateau N and W of the temple (unexcavated)
evidence: 6th-7th c. inscription recording renewal of stucco and painting of the temple (prasada) and a brass image in the monastery (vihara); inscriptions of pilgrims from Ceylon and Samatata
quote: The temple (prdsdda) naturally must have been the same edifice Avhicb w e still have at the present day … remains of this stately building, perhaps one of the largest Saiighanmas tliat ever existed in India, still lie buried beneath the liigli plateau, sti‘etching to a considerable extent to the north and west of the Temple
note: Agrees with Mizutani (08.06.04 = Mahabodhi temple; 08.06.30 = mound N of the temple) and with Cunningham; Bloch tentatively links the inscription's gandhakuti to Xuanzang's large temple W of the Bodhi tree.
Naga worship in ancient Mathura (Vogel); no location of a Xiyu ji place.
